overview_description.description:
ElevateBio is an operator of a portfolio of cell and gene therapy companies intended to develop, manufacture, and commercialize life-transforming medicines.

The company creates a portfolio through partnerships with the world's innovative scientists and inventors as well as it created a centralized facility that integrates all the elements that translate cell and gene therapy R&D into commercially viable therapies quickly and efficiently, enabling patients to get medical products to treat severe diseases.

Vikas Sinha, Mitchell Finer, and David Hallal co-founded ElevateBio in Cambridge, Massachusetts in 2017.

product.name: BaseCamp®
product.description: A cGMP manufacturing and process development facility providing end-to-end capabilities for cell and gene therapy production from concept through commercialization.

product.name: LentiPeak™ Lentiviral Vector Platform
product.description: A suspension-based, scalable lentiviral vector production platform designed for efficient manufacturing of lentiviral vectors for gene and cell therapies.

product.name: Life Edit Gene Editing Platform
product.description: A gene editing technology platform offering a broad range of RNA-guided nucleases, base editors, and reverse transcriptase editors for precise genome modification in cell and gene therapies.

product.name: Cell Therapy Enabling Technologies
product.description: Technology platforms designed to enhance immune cell function and proliferation, overcoming immunosuppressive environments in cell therapies.

identifier.value: RNA, Protein, and Vector Engineering Platforms

product.name: RNA, Protein, and Vector Engineering Platforms
product.description: Integrated platforms for engineering cells, proteins, and vectors essential for the design and construction of cell and gene therapies.

product.name: Analytical Services and Quality Control
product.description: Comprehensive analytical testing and quality control services supporting process development, product release, and regulatory compliance for cell and gene therapies.
